📌 Tampered Hardware Wallets: Why Where You Buy Matters

Main Points
⏺ A hardware wallet is only safe if nobody touched it before you
⏺ Attackers modify genuine devices and resell them as new
⏺ This post explains how the trick works and how to buy safely




1️⃣ Core Idea — A hardware wallet keeps your keys offline. But if the device was opened and altered before it reached you, the attacker may already know your keys.
2️⃣ Why It Happens — Real devices are bought, tampered with, repackaged and sold again through third-party sellers and marketplaces, often at a small discount.
3️⃣ Example — Users in Berlin and Dubai have reported receiving genuine-looking devices that turned out to be modified before sale.
4️⃣ Risk Surface — Marketplace listings, "sealed" boxes from unknown shops, devices that arrive with a recovery phrase card already filled in or a PIN already set.
5️⃣ Practical Rule — Buy only directly from the manufacturer's official store, run its genuineness check on first setup, and always generate a new recovery phrase yourself.
Final Thoughts

Saving a few dollars on a wallet is not worth the coins it will hold. If anything about the box or the setup feels off, don't use the device.

The Repeal Bills Skipped the Line

Israel still has no new government. Its parliament has already started taking apart the outgoing government’s legislative work. 

The morning after Matan Kahana became speaker, the Knesset’s Arrangements Committee voted 12–9 to waive the usual 45-day wait for several repeal bills. The clock was one of the first things the new majority voted to get rid of. 

The Knesset gave preliminary approval to separate bills reversing changes to judicial appointments, the attorney general’s powers and broadcast regulation. 

The judges bill would restore the Israel Bar Association’s two seats on the nine-member selection panel and reinstate the old voting rules. The attorney general bill advanced 63–47. 

It would scrap a law due to take effect in January that lets ministers disregard the attorney general’s legal opinions and gives the governing coalition effective control over who holds the job. The broadcast repeal advanced 63–49. 

The law governing police misconduct investigations is also on the rollback list. Democrats lawmaker Gilad Kariv is expected to chair a temporary committee handling key judicial repeal bills. 

The measures that cleared preliminary votes still need three more readings. Wednesday’s votes show that Eisenkot’s bloc can move bills before it forms a government; they don’t show that it can carry every repeal over the finish line. 

Kahana called for broad agreement. The new majority’s first agreement was that it didn’t need 45 days to look for it.

📣 MEXC shuts down Visa-linked crypto card less than three months after launch 

🌐 Cryptocurrency exchange MEXC has announced that it will discontinue its Global Card payment services on Nov. 18 at 15:30 UTC, less than two weeks after U.S. authorities issued an order restricting its access to the American financial system. The exchange did not identify the issuing partner or specify whether its decision was directly related to the recent enforcement action by the U.S. Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FinCEN).

📊 During the maintenance period, customers could transfer their remaining card balances to their exchange accounts, while transactions initiated before the suspension remained subject to normal settlement procedures. MEXC had initially described the interruption as temporary but has now confirmed that the service will not resume as scheduled.

🔗 Cardholders could receive cashback ranging from 4% to 10%, with monthly rewards capped at up to 800 USDT depending on their eligibility. Applications were already unavailable to U.S. residents under the exchange’s regional restrictions. Customers using the card for recurring payments have been advised to cancel their subscriptions or register alternative payment methods to avoid interruptions once the card becomes inactive.
